report.summary: Analyzed ignore.py chunk 1/2: defines ignore rules, ProjectScope, and env helpers with detailed docstrings and comments.
risks: SCOPE_ALGO_SALT line | high | Changing scope interpretation without bumping salt can cause stale cache hits; relies on developer discipline to update salt. | Check if there is a test or lint rule that enforces salt bump on relevant changes.

_hit method line | medium | Directory rule matching excludes last segment, which may miss some edge cases; behavior is intentional but subtle. | Add test cases for files vs directories with same name.
expand_presets line | medium | Unknown @name presets are passed through, which could cause silent failures if misspelled. | Consider logging a warning for unknown presets.
todos: Consider adding integration tests for cache invalidation when SCOPE_ALGO_SALT changes.
Add explicit test for _hit with '**' patterns to ensure correct fnmatch replacement.
Review env_extra_patterns and env_center for documentation on format expectations.

handoff.purpose: Defines .daedalusignore parsing, ProjectScope zones, and environment variable overrides for per-repo structural ignore rules.

symbols.name: SCOPE_ALGO_SALT
symbols.note: Salt string for scope fingerprint to invalidate caches on interpretation changes.

symbols.name: _Rule
symbols.note: Frozen dataclass representing a single ignore rule with pattern, negated, dir_only, anchored fields.

symbols.name: _parse_line
symbols.note: Parses a single line of .daedalusignore into a _Rule or None (for blank/comment).

symbols.name: IgnoreRules
symbols.note: Dataclass holding ordered list of _Rule, source path, and fingerprint. Provides matches() method for evaluating a repo-relative path.

symbols.name: _fingerprint
symbols.note: Returns first 16 hex chars of SHA256 hash of input text.

symbols.name: load_ignore_rules
symbols.note: Reads .daedalusignore file from given root path and returns IgnoreRules; missing/unreadable returns empty rules.

symbols.name: env_extra_patterns
symbols.note: Returns list of patterns from DAEDALUS_IGNORE environment variable, split by os.pathsep.

symbols.name: _norm_center
symbols.note: Normalizes center paths to repo-relative POSIX, sorted and de-duplicated.

symbols.name: ProjectScope
symbols.note: Frozen dataclass representing concentric scope with center and ignore rules. Provides fingerprint, in_center, center_of, is_shell, describe methods.

symbols.name: env_center
symbols.note: Returns tuple of center paths from DAEDALUS_CENTER environment variable.

symbols.name: IGNORE_PRESETS
symbols.note: Dictionary of named preset strings to tuples of ignore patterns for common test directories/files.

symbols.name: expand_presets
symbols.note: Expands @name entries in a list of patterns using IGNORE_PRESETS; unknown @name passed through.

claims.text: An ignored file is excluded from metrics, but kept for import resolution
claims.why: The actual behavior of ignoring files in metrics vs import resolution is not implemented in this chunk; it only defines the rules and matching logic.

claims.text: it still occupies the file-set indexes
claims.why: No index code present; claim refers to external behavior.

claims.text: it is still parsed, so its own outgoing edges stay honest too
claims.why: Parsing behavior not shown in this chunk.

claims.text: it is withheld from modules, hotspots/module_heat, every clone pass, and the language/LOC summary
claims.why: Withholding logic not present; claim refers to other modules.

claims.text: The cost of that choice is near zero and the payoff is large, because of where scan time actually goes: the per-file parse is ~1.9s of a ~102s warm scan while the clone passes are ~96% of it.
claims.why: Performance numbers are not verifiable from this code chunk; no timing data present.

claims.text: Withholding is therefore never silent -- build_index reports the counts and the rules that produced them, in the same spirit as report.truncated.
claims.why: build_index and report.truncated are not defined in this chunk.

claims.text: BUMP THIS whenever the scope changes what an index CONTAINS rather than which files it covers. The scope fingerprint is the index cache key, and it is built only from the center list and the ignore patterns -- so a change to the *interpretation* of an unchanged center (v2: Python dotted names became package-relative for files under a center root) leaves the key identical and every warm cache, in-process and on disk, keeps serving the OLD graph. That presents as 'the fix did nothing', survives until the next restart, and is exactly the kind of bug that costs an afternoon.
claims.why: The fingerprint construction is present in ProjectScope.fingerprint, but the claim about cache behavior depends on external caching logic (cached_index) not shown here.

claims.text: Unscoped repos are unaffected: index._scope_key gives them a bare path key that never consults this fingerprint, so their cache is not invalidated.
claims.why: index._scope_key is not defined in this chunk.

claims.text: A pattern containing a slash is repo-root anchored, exactly as gitignore defines it: 'docs/vendor' means that path, not any directory named 'vendor' inside any 'docs'.
claims.why: The code sets anchored = '/' in line or raw.lstrip().startswith('/'), which matches the described behavior.

claims.text: Last-match-wins, so ordering is load-bearing and callers must not reorder the file.
claims.why: The matches method iterates over rules in order and updates verdict each time, so last match wins.

claims.text: A directory rule matches every descendant, which is the only reason references/ covers references/a/b.py.
claims.why: In _hit, for anchored rules, if rel starts with pat + '/', it returns True, covering descendants. For unanchored dir_only rules, the last segment is excluded from candidates, but the pattern may match a directory segment; however, the direct descendant coverage is not as explicit as the claim suggests for unanchored rules. The claim is generally correct for anchored rules.

claims.text: Missing/unreadable file -> empty rules.
claims.why: The function catches OSError and returns IgnoreRules with empty rules and empty source/fingerprint.

claims.text: The fingerprint covers the raw file bytes and is folded into the index cache key by cached_index. Without that, editing the ignore file would hand back the previous process-cached index and look like the feature simply did not work.
claims.why: The fingerprint is computed, but its integration with cached_index is not shown in this chunk.

claims.text: DAEDALUS_IGNORE -- os.pathsep-separated patterns, applied after the file. Exists so a scan can be scoped without editing a tracked file.
claims.why: The function reads DAEDALUS_IGNORE, splits by os.pathsep, and returns non-empty patterns. Order of application relative to file is not enforced here but implied.

claims.text: Sorted + de-duplicated: this feeds the cache fingerprint, so two configs that name the same roots in a different order must not build twice.
claims.why: The function uses sorted(set(out)) which sorts and deduplicates.

claims.text: An empty center means the whole repo is the core, which is the historical behaviour and what every un-configured repo keeps getting.
claims.why: in_center returns True if self.center is empty.

claims.text: NOT expressible as in_center: that returns True for every path when no center is declared (the whole repo is the core), which is right for metric decisions and actively wrong for naming ones. A caller written as if scope.in_center(rel): strip_prefix(rel) would read as 'strip everything' on an unconfigured repo and only no-op by accident. This returns None there, so 'no center -> no package root -> no stripping' falls out structurally instead of coincidentally.
claims.why: center_of returns None if no center matches; in_center returns True when self.center is empty. The behavior matches the claim.

claims.text: LONGEST MATCH WINS, not first-sorted. With center=['a', 'a/b'] the file a/b/c.py lives in the *inner* package root, so its package-relative name is c and not b.c. Ties are impossible: two centers that both match and have equal length are the same string, and _norm_center already de-duplicated. Sorted before the length sort so the iteration order is total and never depends on config ordering.
claims.why: The code iterates over sorted(self.center) and updates best if len(c) > len(best). So longest match wins.

claims.text: True when rel is indexed-but-peripheral: outside the declared center, or matched by an ignore rule. These are the files withheld from metrics and not expanded through.
claims.why: The method returns (not self.in_center(rel)) or self.ignore.matches(rel), matching the description.

claims.text: Replace @name entries with their preset patterns, order preserved.
claims.why: The function iterates patterns in order, and for each @name present in IGNORE_PRESETS, extends with preset patterns; otherwise appends the original string.

claims.text: An unknown @name is passed through untouched rather than dropped: a silent no-op would look exactly like a preset that did nothing.
claims.why: If s is not in IGNORE_PRESETS and s is non-empty, it is appended to out. Unknown @name (e.g., '@unknown') is passed through because it won't match any preset.

observations.what: SCOPE_ALGO_SALT is a constant that should be bumped when interpretation changes; the comment explains the risk of cache staleness.
_parse_line handles line endings and comments, but does not handle trailing spaces in the pattern after stripping; the strip is done before checking for '/', which may affect anchored detection.

In _hit, for unanchored dir_only rules, the last segment is excluded from candidates, meaning a directory rule like 'build/' will not match a file named 'build' but also will not match a directory named 'build' if it is the last segment? Actually, it matches any segment except the last, so a path 'a/build/b.py' will match because 'build' is a candidate; but 'build/x.py' will also match because 'build' is a candidate. The claim about 'build/' not matching a FILE named 'build' is correct because the last segment is excluded, so 'build' as a file name is not considered.
The '**' handling in _hit only replaces '**/' with '*', which may not cover all cases (e.g., 'a/**/b' or '**' alone).
load_ignore_rules uses errors='replace' which may mask encoding issues; the fingerprint is computed from text after replacement, so the fingerprint may differ if encoding is wrong.
env_extra_patterns and env_center use os.environ.get; no validation that the patterns are valid.
expand_presets passes through unknown @name patterns; this could lead to silent errors if a user misspells a preset name.
